title: Effect of foliar application of potassium silicate on regulating the biochemical traits of leaves and maintaining kiwifruit quality during cold storage
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Silicon (Si) and potassium (K) are beneficial and essential elements for plants, respectively, and they play important roles in improving the quality and storability of crop products. Therefore, this study evaluated the effects of foliar spraying with potassium silicate (PS) during the kiwifruit growth period on specific leaf biochemical attributes and on the biochemical composition of the fruit, which regulates kiwifruit quality during cold storage. In this study, kiwifruit vines were subjected to different levels of PS (0%, 0.2%, 0.4%, 0.6%) in 2022 and 2023. Fruits were harvested and then transferred to cold storage (0 ± 0.5 °C), and their biochemical characteristics were evaluated at 45-day intervals.

RESULTS

The results indicated that the leaf contents of K, Si, chlorophyll a, total phenolics, and antioxidant capacity were increased by 100%, 190%, 12%, 19%, and 83%, respectively, through a 0.6% PS treatment. At the harvest and storage stages, the fruit's biochemical attributes, including total pectin, total soluble carbohydrates, ratio of total soluble solids to titratable acidity, and greenness of fruit texture, were improved through super treatments (0.4% and 0.6% treatments). Moreover, foliar application of PS significantly delayed fruit softening during cold storage and inhibited (32–40%) polygalacturonase enzyme activity in the fruit texture relative to the control fruits.

CONCLUSION

The results of the present study indicate that foliar application of PS at a concentration of 0.4–0.6% in the first phase of kiwifruit growth can serve as a suitable nutritional solution for enhancing kiwifruit storage quality and postharvest life. © 2025 Society of Chemical Industry.
